shortBio: Automation Architect building intelligent testing systems, autonomous workflows, and exploring Agentic AI.
fullBio:
Back in 2015, my career began with manual testing on enterprise ERP systems. Spending hours running repetitive regression suites taught me an unforgettable lesson: manual testing doesn't just slow releases down; it drains the energy and creativity out of talented engineers. That early friction sparked an obsession with automation—an 11-year journey transforming how teams approach software reliability.

Over the past decade, I've designed scalable end-to-end frameworks, mentored quality engineers into test developers, and stepped into architectural roles where quality is treated as a core engineering discipline rather than an afterthought. Today at emagine, I operate at the frontier of Quality Engineering and Artificial Intelligence—building autonomous testing agents, RAG pipelines, and MCP-integrated workflows using Playwright, LangChain, and modern LLM orchestration.

Beyond writing code and designing pipelines, what truly drives me is developer enablement and team velocity. Whether facilitating sprint ceremonies as a Certified Scrum Master (PSM I, CSM) or open-sourcing AI tools that turn tedious 3-hour tasks into 3-minute wins, my mission remains the same: eliminate mechanical toil so engineers can spend their energy solving meaningful human problems.

principles.title: Automate the Toil, Protect the Craft
principles.description: AI and automation aren't meant to replace human judgment—they're meant to eliminate repetitive grind so engineers can focus on creative problem solving.

principles.title: Shift Left or Pay Later
principles.description: A bug caught during architecture or design costs 10 minutes to fix; a bug caught in production costs a weekend and user trust.

principles.title: AI Speed + Architectural Rigor
principles.description: Move at the speed of modern AI assistants, but ground every implementation in clean design patterns, observable pipelines, and deterministic tests.

principles.title: Agile with Empathy
principles.description: Being a Scrum Master isn't about policing velocity charts—it's about clearing roadblocks, listening closely, and creating an environment where people do their best work.

philosophy: I believe quality starts long before execution — whether through Shift Left principles, AI-assisted workflows, or forging tools that eliminate repetitive work. The goal is always the same: help engineers spend less time on manual effort and more time solving meaningful problems.
